title.en: A new venue with a long contract

text.en: Madring is a new circuit in the IFEMA-Valdebebas area of Madrid, made up of street and non-street sections. Formula 1 announced the deal on 23 January 2024: IFEMA Madrid would organise the Spanish Grand Prix from 2026 to 2035, a period of about ten years. The first race, in 2026, was won by Kimi Antonelli for Mercedes, 4.351 seconds ahead of Max Verstappen, with Lando Norris third; a Virtual Safety Car after Lance Stroll stopped at Turn 20 shaped the pit-stop strategies. As of the sources opened, Madring is therefore an active Formula 1 venue rather than a historical one, and its 2026 race is both its first and, so far, its most recent. A city tourism listing found in a search gives 10-12 September 2027 for the next edition, but that page was not opened.
text.uk: Madring — нова траса в районі IFEMA-Вальдебебас у Мадриді, що поєднує вуличні й невуличні ділянки. Формула 1 оголосила угоду 23 січня 2024 року: IFEMA Madrid організовуватиме Гран прі Іспанії з 2026 по 2035 рік, тобто приблизно десять років. Першу гонку у 2026 році виграв Кімі Антонеллі на Mercedes, випередивши Макса Ферстаппена на 4.351 секунди; третім був Ландо Норріс. Віртуальний автомобіль безпеки після зупинки Ленса Стролла на повороті 20 вплинув на піт-стоп-стратегії. Отже, за відкритими джерелами Madring — діюча траса Формули 1, а не історична, і її гонка 2026 року є одночасно першою та поки що останньою. Туристичний довідник міста, знайдений під час пошуку, називає наступну гонку 10-12 вересня 2027 року, але цю сторінку не відкривали.

limitations: The Reuters race report could not be fetched and the 2027 date comes from a search listing that was not opened, so no claim about 2027 beyond the contract is stated as verified.

The Spanish Motorsport.com article gives 5.47 km and 22 turns, and F1.com's January 2024 announcement 5.47 km with 20 corners (preliminary); F1DB gives 5.416 km and 22 turns. The prose uses no length.
Whether the corner names are 'official' circuit names or media/layout-presentation names was not verified; Motorsport.com (Spain) is the only publisher that ties them to turn numbers.
'Subida de las Cárcavas' is a named climb starting at Turn 6, not a single corner, so it should be reviewed before being placed as a corner name.
The Formula 1 race report states Antonelli won by 4.351 s but also quotes 4.2 s over his nearest rivals; the timed gap 4.351 s is used and matches the existing prose.
The F1 report did not mention the circuit's future; the contract term comes from the 2024 announcement.
